The factor is the ratio of the official Berlin trips per vehicle per day to our own Berlin measurement; it applies to e-scooters everywhere, the range follows from the smallest and largest Berlin quarterly value. Bikes and e-bikes stay measured.

rep.basisIsOperatorsOpenLive: The basis is the operators' open live feeds (GBFS), fetched about every 20 minutes. A trip starts when an available vehicle disappears from the feed (rotating IDs) or reappears more than 150 m away with the same ID. ID rotation at the same spot (≤ 40 m), rebalancing by the operator and pickups of disabled or nearly empty vehicles do not count as trips. Runs more than 45 minutes after the previous one (gaps) and their hours are not included in the trips.
rep.tripsPerDayAreMeasuredTrips: Trips per day are measured trips divided by the observed share of the typical daily profile.{calMethod} Operators without an open feed are missing. Mobility Pulse · {v1}

rep.fleetAllEScootersReportedBy: Fleet = all e-scooters reported by the open feeds in the municipality: available, reserved and disabled, after reconciling duplicate sources. Operators without an open feed are missing, so the check is a lower bound. Status: ok below {v0} %, near from {v0} %, over above 100 % of the cap. Only official figures are checked; calculated figures ({v1}) give only a note, sub-area caps (e.g. Berlin inside the S-Bahn ring) cannot be checked without an area boundary, operators outside the source's complete operator list appear as “not licensed according to source” (no violation). Available ÷ allowed = the operator's bookable vehicles ÷ its allowed number; without a cap per operator, its share of the total cap is shown there. Per city and operator with daily history under Market view › Performance › Availability per city.

rep.zwNote: The outlines are an assumption: derived from the city’s description and roughly simplified, not official data (data/zonen-vermutet.json). Vehicles near the boundary may be assigned wrongly. Fleet = vehicles with a position inside the zone after de-duplication, per collector run; daily values (min, max, mean) for {days} days. If an operator’s feed fails, no zero fleet is recorded. Thresholds and status are shown in the fleet cap monitor.
rep.capZoneChecked: checked against the assumed boundary (± {m} m, derived from the description, not official) · as of {at}
rep.zwLive: No collector log yet: fleet counted directly from the current collector snapshot (one point in time; history follows with the next runs).
zv.rest: rest of the municipality: vehicles outside the assumed sub-areas
zv.live: counted live (not yet in the collector log)
zv.superset: outline deliberately larger than the described area: the fleet is an upper bound, above the cap only a note
zv.noRuns: assumed boundary available, but no fleet of this vehicle type in the feed – not checkable
zv.capsDefn: Fleet = all e-scooters reported by the open feeds in the municipality: available, reserved and disabled, after reconciling duplicate sources. Operators without an open feed are missing, so the check is a lower bound. Status: ok below {v0} %, near from {v0} %, over above 100 % of the cap. Only official figures are checked; calculated figures ({v1}) give only a note. Sub-area caps are checked against assumed boundaries (data/zonen-vermutet.json, derived from the city’s description or map, not official; “rest of the city” = the municipality’s remaining vehicles, share rules per operator against its fleet in the city); without an assumed boundary they cannot be checked. Operators outside the source's complete operator list appear as “not licensed according to source” (no violation). Available ÷ allowed = the operator's bookable vehicles ÷ its allowed number; without a cap per operator, its share of the total cap is shown there. Per city and operator with daily history under Market view › Performance › Availability per city.
